+import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
+import androidx.compose.runtime.getValue
+import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableStateOf
+import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
+import androidx.compose.runtime.setValue
+import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
+import androidx.compose.ui.unit.dp
+import dev.opencode.remote.domain.McpServerInfo
+
+/** H10 (P2 scope): per-session totals + context meter. Weekly aggregation deferred to P4/Room. */
+@OptIn(ExperimentalMaterial3Api::class)
+@Composable
+fun StatsSheet(
+    tokensIn: Long,
+    tokensOut: Long,
+    cost: Double,
+    contextLimit: Long,
+    modelLabel: String,
+) {
+    var open by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
+    TextButton(onClick = { open = true }) {
+        Text(
+            "${fmtK(tokensIn + tokensOut)} · $${"%.4f".format(cost)}",
+            style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
+        )
+    }
+    if (open) {
+        ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = { open = false }) {
+            Column(Modifier.padding(16.dp), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
+                Text("Session usage", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
+                StatRow("Model", modelLabel)
+                StatRow("Input tokens", fmtN(tokensIn))
+                StatRow("Output tokens", fmtN(tokensOut))
+                StatRow("Cost", "$" + "%.4f".format(cost))
+                if (contextLimit > 0) {
+                    val used = tokensIn + tokensOut
+                    val frac = (used.toDouble() / contextLimit).coerceIn(0.0, 1.0)
+                    Text("Context ${fmtK(used)} / ${fmtK(contextLimit)} (${(frac * 100).toInt()}%)")
+                    LinearProgressIndicator(progress = { frac.toFloat() }, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth())
+                } else {
+                    Text("Context limit unknown for this model", style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall)
+                }
+                Text(
+                    "Weekly totals need local history — ships with P4.",
+                    style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
+                    color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline,
+                )
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+private fun fmtN(n: Long): String = "%,d".format(n)
+
+private fun fmtK(n: Long): String = when {
+    n >= 1_000_000 -> "%.1fM".format(n / 1_000_000.0)
+    n >= 1_000 -> "%.1fk".format(n / 1_000.0)
+    else -> "$n"
+}
+
+@Composable
+private fun StatRow(label: String, value: String) {
+    Row(Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween) {
+        Text(label, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)
+        Text(value, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium)
+    }
+}
+
+/** H6 (P2 scope): connectors view — MCP server statuses, toggles deferred to P5. */
+@Composable
+fun ConnectorsScreen(servers: List<McpServerInfo>) {
+    Column(Modifier.padding(16.dp), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
+        Text("Connectors", style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineMedium)
+        if (servers.isEmpty()) {
+            Text("No MCP servers reported by this server.")
+        }
+        servers.forEach { s ->
+            Row(Modifier.fillMaxWidth(), horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween) {
+                Text(s.name, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge)
+                Text(s.status, style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall)
+            }
+        }
+        Text(
+            "Enabling/disabling servers ships with the browser phase (P5).",
+            style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
+            color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline,
+        )
+    }
+}

package dev.opencode.remote.domain

import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow

/** A pending permission request (spec PermissionRequest verbatim, lenient). */
data class PermissionItem(
    val id: String,
    val sessionID: String,
    val permission: String,
    val patterns: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val metadata: Map<String, String> = emptyMap(),
    val always: List<String> = emptyList(),
    val messageID: String? = null,
    val callID: String? = null,
    /** Terminal state after reply (grinev rule): null = awaiting. */
    val replied: String? = null,
)

enum class PermissionReplyKind(val wire: String) { ONCE("once"), ALWAYS("always"), REJECT("reject") }

interface PermissionRepository {
    val pending: Flow<List<PermissionItem>>
    suspend fun refresh(): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun reply(id: String, kind: PermissionReplyKind): Result<Unit>
    fun markRepliedExternally(requestID: String)
}

/** A pending AskUserQuestion request (QuestionInfo verbatim, lenient; V2 folded in). */
data class QuestionOption(val label: String, val description: String = "")

data class QuestionItem(
    val id: String,
    val sessionID: String,
    val header: String,
    val question: String,
    val options: List<QuestionOption>,
    val multiple: Boolean = false,
    val customAllowed: Boolean = false,
)

interface QuestionRepository {
    val pending: Flow<List<QuestionItem>>
    suspend fun refresh(): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun reply(id: String, answers: List<List<String>>): Result<Unit>
    suspend fun reject(id: String): Result<Unit>
    fun markSettledExternally(requestID: String)
}

/** Provider/model/agent/command catalogs (server-driven pickers). */
data class ModelInfo(
    val id: String,
    val name: String,
    val contextLimit: Long = 0,
)

data class ProviderInfo(
    val id: String,
    val name: String,
    val models: List<ModelInfo>,
)

data class AgentInfo(
    val name: String,
    val description: String = "",
    val mode: String = "all",
)

data class CommandInfo(
    val name: String,
    val description: String = "",
    val source: String = "",
)

data class McpServerInfo(
    val name: String,
    val status: String,
)

interface CatalogRepository {
    val providers: Flow<List<ProviderInfo>>
    val agents: Flow<List<AgentInfo>>
    val commands: Flow<List<CommandInfo>>
    val mcpServers: Flow<List<McpServerInfo>>
    val toolIds: Flow<List<String>>
    suspend fun refresh(): Result<Unit>
}

/** Per-session model/agent/effort memory (grapeot pattern). */
data class SessionPrefs(
    val modelID: String? = null,
    val providerID: String? = null,
    val variant: String? = null,
    val agent: String? = null,
)

/** Shared active-profile API access for P2 repos (mirrors ChatRepositoryImpl.Holder). */
internal suspend fun ServerRepository.activeApi(): ApiFactory.BoundApi? {
    val id = activeProfileId.first() ?: return null
    val profile = profiles.first().firstOrNull { it.id == id } ?: return null
    return ApiFactory.bound(profile, getPassword(profile.id))
}

# multiplatform-markdown-renderer

[](#multiplatform-markdown-renderer)

Render Markdown as native Compose UI — one API, every platform.

[![CI status](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/workflows/CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/actions) [![Maven Central version](https://camo.githubusercontent.)](https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/com.mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://camo.githubusercontent.)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer) [![Apache 2.0 license](https://camo.githubusercontent.com/f33da71a29405001aa02da9ecc600166564fbf91b075090f06daf1a0012969a3/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f62616467652f6c6963656e73652d417061636865253230322e302d626c75653f7374796c653d666c61742d737175617265)](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/blob/develop/LICENSE)

 ![A markdown String is parsed by JetBrains Markdown into an AST, mapped through overridable MarkdownComponents, and rendered as Compose Multiplatform UI on Android, iOS, Desktop, Web and macOS.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/develop/art/hero-light.svg)

[Quickstart](#quickstart) • [Showcase](#showcase) • [Reference](#reference) • [Migration](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/blob/develop/MIGRATION.md) • [Changelog](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/blob/develop/CHANGELOG.md)

🧩 **Every platform**

Android, iOS, Desktop (JVM), Web (Wasm / JS) and macOS from one `commonMain` call.

⚡ **Async by default**

`rememberMarkdownState` parses off the composition; `retainState = true` keeps content visible while re-parsing.

🎨 **Material 2 and 3**

Themed defaults from `-m2` / `-m3`; override with `markdownColor()` and `markdownTypography()`.

🧱 **Every element overridable**

`MarkdownComponents` maps each AST node to a `@Composable` you control.

📊 **Full GFM**

Tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks and GitHub alerts, out of the box.

📡 **Built for streaming**

`rememberStreamingMarkdownState()` appends chunks and re-parses only the unstable tail.

## Quickstart

[](#quickstart)

**1 — Add the dependency.** Pick the module matching your Material theme:

dependencies {
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer:0.43.0")
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-m3:0.43.0") // or -m2
}

**2 — Render.** Import `Markdown` from `com.mikepenz.markdown.m3` (or `.m2`):

import com.mikepenz.markdown.m3.Markdown

Markdown(
    """
    # Hello Markdown
    - Bullet points
    - \*\*Bold\*\* and \*italic\* text
    \[Check out this link\](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer)
    """.trimIndent()
)

**3 — Hoist the parse for anything non-trivial.** `rememberMarkdownState` parses asynchronously and survives recomposition:

val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(markdown)
Markdown(markdownState)

Full configuration — custom components, image loading, syntax highlighting, extended spans — is in the [Reference](#reference) below.

### What's included 🚀

[](#whats-included-)

-   **Cross-platform Markdown Rendering** - Works on Android, iOS, Desktop, and Web
-   **Material Design Integration** - Seamless integration with Material 2 and Material 3 themes
-   **Rich Markdown Support** - Renders headings, lists, code blocks, tables, images, and more
-   **Syntax Highlighting** - Optional code syntax highlighting for various programming languages
-   **Image Loading** - Flexible image loading with Coil2 and Coil3 integration
-   **Customization Options** - Extensive customization for colors, typography, components, and more
-   **Performance Optimized** - Efficient rendering with lazy loading support for large documents
-   **Extended Text Spans** - Support for advanced text styling with extended spans
-   **Lightweight** - Minimal dependencies and optimized for performance

## Setup

[](#setup)

### Using Gradle

[](#using-gradle)

Choose the appropriate configuration based on your project type:

**Multiplatform**

For multiplatform projects, add these dependencies to your `build.gradle.kts`:

dependencies {
    // Core library
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer:${version}")

    // Choose ONE of the following based on your Material theme:

    // For Material 2 themed apps
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-m2:${version}")

    // OR for Material 3 themed apps
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-m3:${version}")
}

**JVM (Desktop)**

For JVM-only projects, add this dependency:

dependencies {
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-jvm:${version}")
}

**Android**

For Android-only projects, add this dependency:

dependencies {
    implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-android:${version}")
}

Important

Since version 0.13.0, the core library does not depend on a Material theme. You must include either the `-m2` or `-m3` module to get access to the default styling.

## Usage

[](#usage)

### Basic Usage

[](#basic-usage)

The most basic usage is to simply pass your markdown string to the `Markdown` composable:

// In your composable (use the appropriate Markdown implementation for your theme)
Markdown(
    """
    # Hello Markdown
    This is a simple markdown example with:
    - Bullet points
    - \*\*Bold text\*\*
    - \*Italic text\*
    \[Check out this link\](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer)
    """.trimIndent()
)

Note

Import either `com.mikepenz.markdown.m3.Markdown` for Material 3 or `com.mikepenz.markdown.m2.Markdown` for Material 2 themed applications.

Note

By default, when the markdown `content` changes, the component will display a loading state while parsing the new content. To keep the previous content visible during updates and avoid showing the loading state, set `retainState` to `true`.

**Advanced Usage**

### `rememberMarkdownState`

[](#remembermarkdownstate)

For better performance, especially with larger markdown content, use `rememberMarkdownState` or move the parsing of the markdown into your viewmodel:

val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(markdown)
Markdown(markdownState)

> \[!NOTE\]  
> Since version 0.33.0, markdown content is parsed asynchronously by default, resulting in a loading state being displayed prior to the parsing result. The `rememberMarkdownState` function offers the ability to require immediate parsing with the `immediate` parameter, but this is not advised as it might block the composition of the UI.

// Default asynchronous parsing (recommended)
val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(markdown)

// Force immediate parsing (not recommended)
val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(markdown, immediate \= true)

#### Retaining State During Updates

[](#retaining-state-during-updates)

By default, when the markdown content changes, the component shows a loading state while parsing the new content. You can use the `retainState` parameter to keep the previous rendered content visible while the new content is being parsed:

// Retain previous content during updates (avoids showing loading state)
val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(
    markdown,
    retainState \= true
)
Markdown(markdownState)

// With dynamic content loading
val markdownState \= rememberMarkdownState(
    key, // key that triggers re-parsing
    retainState \= true
) {
    "\# Dynamic content $counter"
}
Markdown(markdownState)

This is particularly useful when content updates frequently or when you want to avoid flickering between the old content and the loading state.

### Lazy Loading for Large Documents

[](#lazy-loading-for-large-documents)

Since version 0.33.0, the library supports rendering large markdown documents efficiently using `LazyColumn` instead of `Column`. This is particularly useful for very long markdown content.

Markdown(
    markdownState \= markdownState,
    success \= { state, components, modifier \->
        LazyMarkdownSuccess(state, components, modifier, contentPadding \= PaddingValues(16.dp))
    },
    modifier \= Modifier.fillMaxSize()
)

### Parse Markdown in VM

[](#parse-markdown-in-vm)

> \[!NOTE\]  
> This approach is also advised if you want to retain scroll position even when navigating away See: [#374](https://github.com/mikepenz/multiplatform-markdown-renderer/issues/374) Retaining state in the VM ensures parsing will not have to be done again, and the component can be immediately filled.

// In the VM setup the flow to parse the markdown
val markdownFlow \= parseMarkdownFlow("\# Markdown")
    .stateIn(lifecycleScope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, State.Loading())

// In the Composable use the flow
val state by markdownFlow.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
Markdown(state)

### Parse Markdown synchronously

[](#parse-markdown-synchronously)

If you want to pre-parse content before showing the UI and hand the result to `Markdown` without any Flow/StateFlow machinery, use `parseMarkdown`. It parses on the calling thread and returns the final, immutable `State` directly (`State.Success` on success, or `State.Error` on failure).

// Parse ahead of time and pass the already-parsed state to the Composable
val state \= parseMarkdown("\# Markdown")
Markdown(state)

> \[!NOTE\]  
> Parsing happens on the calling thread. For large documents consider invoking this off the main thread.

The library offers the ability to modify different behaviour when rendering the markdown.

### Provided custom style

[](#provided-custom-style)

Markdown(
    content,
    colors \= markdownColor(text \= Color.Red),
    typography \= markdownTypography(h1 \= MaterialTheme.typography.body1)
)

### Disable Animation

[](#disable-animation)

By default, the `MarkdownText` animates size changes (if images are loaded).

Markdown(
    content,
    animations \= markdownAnimations(
        animateTextSize \= {
            this
            /\*\* No animation \*/
        }
    ),
)

### Extended spans

[](#extended-spans)

Starting with 0.16.0 the library includes support for [extended-spans](https://github.com/saket/extended-spans).

> The library was integrated to make it multiplatform-compatible. All credits for its functionality go to [Saket Narayan](https://github.com/saket).

It is not enabled by default, however you can enable it quickly by configuring the `extendedSpans` for your `Markdown` composeable. Define the `ExtendedSpans` you want to apply (including optionally your own custom ones) and return it.

Markdown(
    content,
    extendedSpans \= markdownExtendedSpans {
        val animator \= rememberSquigglyUnderlineAnimator()
        remember {
            ExtendedSpans(
                RoundedCornerSpanPainter(),
                SquigglyUnderlineSpanPainter(animator \= animator)
            )
        }
    }
)

### Extend Annotated string handling

[](#extend-annotated-string-handling)

The library already handles a significant amount of different tokens, however not all. To allow special integrations expand this, you can pass in a custom `annotator` to the `Markdown` composeable. This `annotator` allows you to customize existing handled tokens, but also add new ones.

Markdown(
    content,
    annotator \= markdownAnnotator { content, child \->
        if (child.type \== GFMElementTypes.STRIKETHROUGH) {
            append("Replaced you :)")
            true // return true to consume this ASTNode child
        } else false
    }
)

### Adjust List Ordering

[](#adjust-list-ordering)

// Use the bullet list symbol from the original markdown
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalBulletListHandler provides { type, bullet, index, listNumber, depth \-> "$bullet " }) {
    Markdown(content)
}

// Replace the ordered list symbol with \`A.)\` instead.
CompositionLocalProvider(LocalOrderedListHandler provides { type, bullet, index, listNumber, depth \-> "A.) " }) {
    Markdown(content, Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(16.dp).verticalScroll(scrollState))
}

### Custom Components

[](#custom-components)

Since v0.9.0 it is possible to provide custom components, instead of the default ones. This can be done by providing the components `MarkdownComponents` to the `Markdown` composable.

Use the `markdownComponents()` to keep defaults for non overwritten components.

The `MarkdownComponent` will expose access to the `content: String`, `node: ASTNode`, `typography: MarkdownTypography`, offering full flexibility.

// Simple adjusted paragraph with different Modifier.
val customParagraphComponent: MarkdownComponent \= {
    Box(modifier \= Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) {
        MarkdownParagraph(it.content, it.node, Modifier.align(Alignment.CenterEnd))
    }
}

// Full custom paragraph example 
val customParagraphComponentComplex: MarkdownComponent \= {
    // build a styled paragraph. (util function provided by the library)
    val styledText \= buildAnnotatedString {
        pushStyle(LocalMarkdownTypography.current.paragraph.toSpanStyle())
        buildMarkdownAnnotatedString(it.content, it.node, annotatorSettings())
        pop()
    }

    // define the \`Text\` composable
    Text(
        styledText,
        textAlign \= TextAlign.End
    )
}

// Define the \`Markdown\` composable and pass in the custom paragraph component
Markdown(
    content,
    components \= markdownComponents(
        paragraph \= customParagraphComponent // customParagraphComponentComplex
    )
)

Another example to of a custom component is changing the rendering of an unordered list.

// Define a custom component for rendering unordered list items in Markdown
val customUnorderedListComponent: MarkdownComponent \= {
    // Use the MarkdownListItems composable to render the list items
    MarkdownListItems(it.content, it.node, depth \= 0) { startNumber, index, child \->
        // Render an icon for the bullet point with a green tint
        Icon(
            imageVector \= icon,
            tint \= Color.Green,
            contentDescription \= null,
            modifier \= Modifier.size(20.dp),
        )
    }
}

// Define the \`Markdown\` composable and pass in the custom unorderedList component
Markdown(
    content,
    components \= markdownComponents(
        unorderedList \= customUnorderedListComponent
    )
)

### Table Support

[](#table-support)

Starting with 0.30.0, the library includes support for rendering tables in markdown. The `Markdown` composable will automatically handle table elements in your markdown content.

val markdown \= """
| Header 1 | Header 2 |
|----------|----------|
| Cell 1   | Cell 2   |
| Cell 3   | Cell 4   |
""".trimIndent()

Markdown(markdown)

### Alert Support

[](#alert-support)

The library renders [GitHub alerts](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/16925) — `NOTE`, `TIP`, `IMPORTANT`, `WARNING` and `CAUTION` — as an accent bar with an icon and a title.

val markdown \= """
\> \[!NOTE\]
\> Useful information that users should know, even when skimming content.
""".trimIndent()

Markdown(markdown)

The accent colors, dimensions and paddings are grouped into dedicated models, the title style is exposed via `markdownTypography(alertTitle = ...)`:

Markdown(
    markdown,
    colors \= markdownColor(alert \= markdownAlertColors(note \= Color.Blue)),
    dimens \= markdownDimens(alert \= markdownAlertDimens(barThickness \= 2.dp)),
    padding \= markdownPadding(alert \= markdownAlertPadding(iconSpacing \= 12.dp)),
)

The icons are swappable via `LocalMarkdownAlertIcons`:

CompositionLocalProvider(
    LocalMarkdownAlertIcons provides markdownAlertIcons(note \= Icons.Outlined.Info)
) {
    Markdown(markdown)
}

To fully replace the rendering, override the `alert` component through `markdownComponents()`.

## Streaming

[](#streaming)

For content that arrives in chunks — an LLM response, a network stream — use `rememberStreamingMarkdownState()`. It is append-only: each `append` re-parses only the unstable tail of the document rather than the whole string.

val streamingMarkdownState \= rememberStreamingMarkdownState()

LaunchedEffect(chunkFlow) {
    chunkFlow.collect { chunk \-> streamingMarkdownState.append(chunk) }
}

Markdown(streamingMarkdownState \= streamingMarkdownState)

If the chunks already arrive as a `Flow<String>`, `collectAsStreamingMarkdownState()` does the collecting for you:

val streamingMarkdownState \= chunkFlow.collectAsStreamingMarkdownState()
Markdown(streamingMarkdownState \= streamingMarkdownState)

`StreamingMarkdownState.snapshot` exposes the split as a `StateFlow<Snapshot>` with `stableAst` and `unstableAstTail`, if you need to observe it. See `StreamingMarkDownPage` in the sample for a working example including render statistics.

### Image Loading

[](#image-loading)

To configure image loading, the library offers different implementations, to offer great flexibility for the respective integration. After adding the dependency, the chosen image transformer implementation has to be passed to the `Markdown` API.

Note

Please refer to the official documentation for the specific image loading integration you are using (e.g., coil3) on how to adjust its behavior.

#### coil3

[](#coil3)

// Offers coil3 (Coil3ImageTransformerImpl)
implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-coil3:${version}")

Markdown(
    MARKDOWN,
    imageTransformer \= Coil3ImageTransformerImpl,
)

#### coil2

[](#coil2)

// Offers coil2 (Coil2ImageTransformerImpl)
implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-coil2:${version}")

Markdown(
    MARKDOWN,
    imageTransformer \= Coil2ImageTransformerImpl,
)

### Syntax Highlighting

[](#syntax-highlighting)

The library (introduced with 0.27.0) offers optional support for syntax highlighting via the [Highlights](https://github.com/SnipMeDev/Highlights) project. This support is not included in the core, and can be enabled by adding the `multiplatform-markdown-renderer-code` dependency.

implementation("com.mikepenz:multiplatform-markdown-renderer-code:${version}")

Once added, the `Markdown` has to be configured to use the alternative code highlighter.

// Use default color scheme
Markdown(
    MARKDOWN,
    components \= markdownComponents(
        codeBlock \= highlightedCodeBlock,
        codeFence \= highlightedCodeFence,
    )
)

// ADVANCED: Customize Highlights library by defining different theme
val isDarkTheme \= isSystemInDarkTheme()
val highlightsBuilder \= remember(isDarkTheme) {
    Highlights.Builder().theme(SyntaxThemes.atom(darkMode \= isDarkTheme))
}
Markdown(
    MARKDOWN,
    components \= markdownComponents(
        codeBlock \= {
            MarkdownHighlightedCodeBlock(
                content \= it.content,
                node \= it.node,
                highlightsBuilder \= highlightsBuilder,
                showHeader \= true, // optional enable header with code language + copy button
            )
        },
        codeFence \= {
            MarkdownHighlightedCodeFence(
                content \= it.content,
                node \= it.node,
                highlightsBuilder \= highlightsBuilder,
                showHeader \= true, // optional enable header with code language + copy button
            )
        },
    )
)

## Dependencies

[](#dependencies)

This library uses the following key dependencies:

-   [JetBrains Markdown](https://github.com/JetBrains/markdown/) - Multiplatform Markdown processor for parsing markdown content
-   [Compose Multiplatform](https://github.com/JetBrains/compose-multiplatform) - For cross-platform UI rendering
-   [Extended Spans](https://github.com/saket/extended-spans) - For advanced text styling (integrated as multiplatform)
-   [Highlights](https://github.com/SnipMeDev/Highlights) - For code syntax highlighting (optional)

package dev.opencode.remote.chat

import androidx.compose.runtime.Composable
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.Modifier
import com.mikepenz.markdown.compose.Markdown
import com.mikepenz.markdown.compose.components.markdownComponents
import com.mikepenz.markdown.compose.elements.highlightedCodeFence
import com.mikepenz.markdown.m3.markdownColor
import com.mikepenz.markdown.m3.markdownTypography

/**
 * Agent text renderer (P2): full markdown (tables, lists, links, GFM alerts) +
 * highlighted code fences with language header + copy button (spec §3).
 * 0.41.0 pinned: last line readable by Kotlin 2.2 (stdlib 2.3.21); no streaming
 * state API in this line, so updates re-parse with retained state (no flicker).
 */
@Composable
fun MarkdownText(text: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
    val components = remember {
        markdownComponents(codeFence = highlightedCodeFence)
    }
    Markdown(
        content = text,
        colors = markdownColor(),
        typography = markdownTypography(),
        components = components,
        retainState = true,
        modifier = modifier,
    )
}

 )

+package dev.opencode.remote.chat
+
+import android.content.Context
+import android.graphics.BitmapFactory
+import android.graphics.Bitmap
+import android.net.Uri
+import android.util.Base64
+import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream
+
+/** Staged attachment (H2): content resolved lazily at send time. */
+data class StagedAttachment(
+    val id: String,
+    val uri: String,
+    val filename: String,
+    val mime: String,
+    val sizeBytes: Long,
+)
+
+data class ResolvedAttachment(
+    val filename: String,
+    val mime: String,
+    val dataUrl: String,
+)
+
+/**
+ * Pure staging helpers (unit-tested). Compression policy (settings):
+ * quality 0 = original bytes; 1 = JPEG q85 maxDim; 2 = JPEG q70 maxDim.
+ */
+object Attachments {
+
+    fun isImage(mime: String): Boolean = mime.startsWith("image/")
+
+    fun targetDim(maxDim: Int): Int = maxDim.coerceIn(320, 4096)
+
+    fun jpegQuality(quality: Int): Int = when (quality) {
+        1 -> 85
+        2 -> 70
+        else -> 70
+    }
+
+    fun buildDataUrl(mime: String, bytes: ByteArray): String =
+        "data:$mime;base64," + Base64.encodeToString(bytes, Base64.NO_WRAP)
+
+    /** Downscale + JPEG-encode. Returns null when the source can't be decoded. */
+    fun compressImage(src: ByteArray, maxDim: Int, quality: Int): ByteArray? {
+        val opts = BitmapFactory.Options().apply { inJustDecodeBounds = true }
+        BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray(src, 0, src.size, opts)
+        if (opts.outWidth <= 0 || opts.outHeight <= 0) return null
+        var sample = 1
+        val longest = maxOf(opts.outWidth, opts.outHeight)
+        while (longest / sample > maxDim) sample *= 2
+        val decode = BitmapFactory.Options().apply { inSampleSize = sample }
+        val bmp = BitmapFactory.decodeByteArray(src, 0, src.size, decode) ?: return null
+        val scaled = if (maxOf(bmp.width, bmp.height) > maxDim) {
+            val f = maxDim.toFloat() / maxOf(bmp.width, bmp.height)
+            Bitmap.createScaledBitmap(bmp, (bmp.width * f).toInt(), (bmp.height * f).toInt(), true)
+        } else bmp
+        val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
+        scaled.compress(Bitmap.CompressFormat.JPEG, jpegQuality(quality), out)
+        if (scaled !== bmp) bmp.recycle()
+        return out.toByteArray()
+    }
+}
+
+/** Resolve a staged attachment to a sendable data-URL part (IO thread). */
+fun resolveAttachment(
+    ctx: Context,
+    att: StagedAttachment,
+    quality: Int,
+    maxDim: Int,
+    maxBytes: Long,
+): ResolvedAttachment? {
+    if (att.sizeBytes > maxBytes && !Attachments.isImage(att.mime)) return null
+    val uri = Uri.parse(att.uri) ?: return null
+    val src = ctx.contentResolver.openInputStream(uri)?.use { it.readBytes() } ?: return null
+    if (src.size > maxBytes * 4) return null // sanity: never stage absurd blobs
+    val mime = att.mime.ifBlank { "application/octet-stream" }
+    val bytes = if (Attachments.isImage(mime) && quality > 0) {
+        Attachments.compressImage(src, Attachments.targetDim(maxDim), quality)
+            ?: return null
+    } else src
+    if (bytes.size > maxBytes) return null
+    val finalMime = if (Attachments.isImage(mime) && quality > 0) "image/jpeg" else mime
+    return ResolvedAttachment(att.filename, finalMime, Attachments.buildDataUrl(finalMime, bytes))
+}

+import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
+
+@HiltViewModel
+class ProjectsViewModel @Inject constructor(
+    private val projects: ProjectRepository,
+) : ViewModel() {
+    val state = projects.projects
+        .stateIn(viewModelScope, SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000), emptyList())
+
+    fun save(existing: Project?, name: String, directories: String, instructions: String, memory: String) {
+        viewModelScope.launch {
+            projects.upsert(
+                (existing ?: Project(id = UUID.randomUUID().toString(), name = "")).copy(
+                    name = name.trim(),
+                    directories = directories.split("\n").map { it.trim() }.filter { it.isNotEmpty() },
+                    instructions = instructions,
+                    memoryNote = memory,
+                ),
+            )
+        }
+    }
+
+    fun delete(id: String) {
+        viewModelScope.launch { projects.delete(id) }
+    }
+}
+
+/** H11: project manager — CRUD + directories + instructions + memory. */
+@Composable
+fun ProjectsScreen(vm: ProjectsViewModel = hiltViewModel()) {
+    val list by vm.state.collectAsStateWithLifecycle()
+    var editing by remember { mutableStateOf<Project?>(null) }
+    var adding by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
+    Scaffold(
+        modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(),
+        topBar = { Text("Projects", style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineMedium, modifier = Modifier.statusBarsPadding().padding(16.dp)) },
+        floatingActionButton = { FloatingActionButton(onClick = { adding = true }) { Text("+") } },
+    ) { inner ->
+        LazyColumn(
+            Modifier.padding(inner).navigationBarsPadding().fillMaxSize(),
+            verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp),
+        ) {
+            items(list, key = { it.id }) { p ->
+                Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(horizontal = 16.dp)) {
+                    Column(Modifier.padding(16.dp), verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(4.dp)) {
+                        Text(p.name, style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)
+                        if (p.directories.isNotEmpty()) {
+                            Text(p.directories.joinToString("\n"), style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall)
+                        }
+                        Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
+                            OutlinedButton(onClick = { editing = p }) { Text("Edit") }
+                            OutlinedButton(onClick = { vm.delete(p.id) }) { Text("Delete") }
+                        }
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    if (adding || editing != null) {
+        ProjectEditor(
+            existing = editing,
+            onDismiss = { adding = false; editing = null },
+            onSave = { n, d, i, m ->
+                vm.save(editing, n, d, i, m)
+                adding = false; editing = null
+            },
+        )
+    }
+}
+
+@Composable
+private fun ProjectEditor(
+    existing: Project?,
+    onDismiss: () -> Unit,
+    onSave: (name: String, dirs: String, instructions: String, memory: String) -> Unit,
+) {
+    var name by remember { mutableStateOf(existing?.name ?: "") }
+    var dirs by remember { mutableStateOf(existing?.directories?.joinToString("\n") ?: "") }
+    var instructions by remember { mutableStateOf(existing?.instructions ?: "") }
+    var memory by remember { mutableStateOf(existing?.memoryNote ?: "") }
+    AlertDialog(
+        onDismissRequest = onDismiss,
+        title = { Text(if (existing == null) "New project" else "Edit project") },
+        text = {
+            Column(verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp)) {
+                OutlinedTextField(name, { name = it }, label = { Text("Name") })
+                OutlinedTextField(dirs, { dirs = it }, label = { Text("Directories (one per line)") })
+                OutlinedTextField(instructions, { instructions = it }, label = { Text("Instructions") })
+                OutlinedTextField(memory, { memory = it }, label = { Text("Memory note") })
+            }
+        },
+        confirmButton = {
+            Button(onClick = { onSave(name, dirs, instructions, memory) }, enabled = name.isNotBlank()) {
+                Text("Save")
+            }
+        },
+        dismissButton = { TextButton(onClick = onDismiss) { Text("Cancel") } },
+    )
+}

+package dev.opencode.remote.chat
+
+import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
+import org.junit.Assert.assertNull
+import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
+import org.junit.Test
+
+/** Pure staging helpers (H2). Bitmap paths need a device — verified live instead. */
+class AttachmentsTest {
+
+    @Test
+    fun dataUrlShape() {
+        val url = Attachments.buildDataUrl("image/jpeg", byteArrayOf(1, 2, 3))
+        assertTrue(url.startsWith("data:image/jpeg;base64,"))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun imageDetection() {
+        assertTrue(Attachments.isImage("image/png"))
+        assertTrue(Attachments.isImage("image/jpeg"))
+        assertTrue(!Attachments.isImage("application/pdf"))
+        assertTrue(!Attachments.isImage(""))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun qualityAndDimBounds() {
+        assertEquals(85, Attachments.jpegQuality(1))
+        assertEquals(70, Attachments.jpegQuality(2))
+        assertEquals(1600, Attachments.targetDim(1600))
+        assertEquals(4096, Attachments.targetDim(99_999))
+        assertEquals(320, Attachments.targetDim(10))
+    }
+
+    @Test
+    fun corruptImageReturnsNull() {
+        assertNull(Attachments.compressImage(byteArrayOf(0, 1, 2, 3), 1600, 2))
+        assertNull(Attachments.compressImage(byteArrayOf(), 1600, 2))
+    }
+}

+# SPEC — P3 attachments / voice / projects / vim
+
+Source of truth: `docs/grand-plan.md` §7. Implements: H2 (attachments), H4-dictation (voice mode deferred —
+see §5), H5 (memory toggle wiring), H11 (projects per D1), H13 kickoff (vim scope + spike, non-blocking).
+
+## 1. Attachments (H2)
+
+- Composer `+` button → sheet: Take photo (CameraX or `TakePicture` contract) / Choose image (Photo Picker,
+  no storage perm) / Choose file (SAF `OpenDocument`, any mime).
+- Staging: chips above composer with thumb/name/size + × remove. Images downscaled + JPEG-compressed
+  client-side per settings (max dimension, quality) BEFORE base64; files ≤ setting cap (default 10MB,
+  refuse larger with reason). HEIC/PNG → JPEG convert for photos.
+- Send: `FilePartInput{type:"file", mime, filename, url:"data:<mime>;base64,..."}` appended after the
+  text part (doc 07 probe: verified round-trip). Mixed text+files in one `prompt_async`.
+- Thread render: image parts → Coil thumbnail, tap → zoom/pan viewer (P3 basic viewer: full-screen
+  pan/zoom, share via system sheet). Non-image files → file card (name/mime).
+- Settings honored: image compression (off/light/medium), max dimension, camera resolution.
+
+## 2. Voice dictation (H4-dictation)
+
+- Composer mic button → platform `SpeechRecognizer` (on-device if available) with partial results
+  streamed into the composer text; error states (no speech, no permission) inline.
+  Runtime `RECORD_AUDIO` request with rationale (X5 aggressive list covers it).
+- Full-duplex voice MODE (conversation) → DEFERRED (§5): needs TTS + turn-taking + audio session
+  management; own workstream after P4.
+
+## 3. Projects (H11, D1)
+
+- Client-side `Project` entity: `{id, name, directories[], instructions, memoryNote}` stored in
+  DataStore (Room deferred to P4; DataStore JSON list suffices for P3 scale).
+- Sessions screen: project filter chips (All + projects); new-session sheet offers project attach
+  (sets default directory + injects instructions/memory as `system` prompt on first send of session).
+- Projects manager screen (from Sessions overflow): CRUD + directory multi-add (via server `/project`
+  worktree picker) + instructions/memory editors.
+- H5 memory toggle: per-message effect = include/exclude the project's memoryNote (+ global simple-memory
+  note TBD) from the `system` injection. Composer status row shows memory chip state (chip UI in P3,
+  injection log line in debug).
+
+## 4. Vim workstream kickoff (H13, non-blocking)
+
+- Spike: survey Compose vim options (no known mature lib — expect custom `InputConnection` wrapper
+  around the composer `TextFieldValue` + mode state machine). Deliverable: `docs/vim-spike.md` with
+  approach + effort estimate + maximal-scope breakdown (normal/insert/visual, motions+text objects,
+  registers, macros, marks/jumps, `:s`, counts). NO composer changes in P3 (parallel track).
+
+## 5. Explicit non-goals / deferrals
+
+- Voice MODE (full duplex), audio messages (record/play) → post-P4 workstream.
+- Room (weekly stats store, message cache) → P4 with push bridge.
+- Vim implementation → own workstream after spike approval.
+- Image zoom viewer: basic pan/zoom + share in P3; annotate/crop later.
+
+## 6. Acceptance
+
+1. Photo → staged chip → send → server thread shows file part (verify via GET message mime/filename).
+2. Gallery image + SAF file stage/send the same way; oversize file refused with reason.
+3. Compression settings change resulting upload bytes (spot-check sizes).
+4. Mic → dictated text appears in composer; denied perm → rationale + settings deep-link.
+5. Project CRUD; session attached to project sends with `system` injection (verify via OkHttp body log).
+6. Memory toggle flips injection on/off.
+7. Vim spike doc written with estimate; no composer regression (existing tests green).
+8. Tests: compression/staging VM tests, project repo tests, MockWebServer (file part body shape).
+   Screenshots: attach sheet, staged chips, viewer, dictation, projects screens.
+
+## 7. Review gate
+
+Tests green · emulator screenshots · live file-part round-trip vs server · grand-plan cross-check
+(H2, H4-dictation, H5, H11, H13-spike) · user review.

input.prompt: Read-only research spike for full vim emulation in a Jetpack Compose TextField (Android, minSdk 26). Questions: (1) Is there ANY mature library for vim motions/modes in Compose (search GitHub via gh_grep knowledge: patterns like 'vim' in Kotlin Compose repos, 'VimInputConnection', 'vim motion state machine')? (2) If custom: outline the architecture — custom InputConnection wrapper vs TextFieldValue transformation, how to handle modes (normal/insert/visual), counts, text objects (iw/ap), registers "0-9, macros q/@, marks, jumps, :s substitute, :w/:q semantics for a chat composer (send/clear). (3) Effort estimate in days for maximal scope, and a phased breakdown (core motions → text objects → registers/macros → ex commands). Return findings + URLs. No edits.

Source of truth: grand-plan.md (D-Vim). Status: SPIKE COMPLETE, implementation not started.

## 1. Library survey: nothing exists

- GitHub repo search `vim jetpack compose kotlin` → 1 irrelevant result (Vimystry, a video app).
- Known ecosystem: IdeaVim (IntelliJ, Swing — not reusable), `vim` emulators for Android
  keyboards (e.g. unexpected-keyboard has some motions, wrong layer), Termux vim (terminal, wrong layer).
- Conclusion (matches plan assumption): **custom implementation required**.

## 2. Architecture

  `(text: String, cursor: Int)` → `(text, cursor, mode)` transitions. UI binds to Compose

  `Modifier.onPreviewKeyEvent` for normal-mode keys (hjkl etc. arrive as key events when the
  field is focused; printable-chars path stays on the IME in insert mode).
- Do NOT fight the IME: insert mode = stock Compose text field (IME does composition,
  autocorrect, predictions). Normal/visual modes intercept hardware/software key events at the
  Compose layer and mutate TextFieldValue programmatically.
- `:w` = send, `:q` = clear+blur, `:wq` = send, `:s/a/b/` = substitute on composer text,
  `:e!` = clear. Ex line = same text field prefixed with `:` (mode=commandline).
- Registers `"0-9a-z`: in-memory map in the VM (persist named registers in DataStore later).
  Macros `q{reg}` record key-event stream; `@{reg}` replays through the same transition function
  (pure function ⇒ replay is trivially correct).
- Marks `m{a-z}` + jumps `'{a-z}`: per-composer-position map; jumps across messages not needed
  (composer-only scope). Counts prefix all motions/operators. Text objects `iw/aw/i(/a(/i{/a{ etc.
  via word/sentence/bracket scanners over the String (no LSP needed).

## 3. Phased breakdown (maximal scope)

- V1 (core, ~4–6 days): modes normal/insert/visual(+line), hjkl/wbe/ge/$/0/^/gg/G/fFtT;,./,
  i/a/I/A/o/O, x/X/s/S/r, dd/yy/p/P/u/Ctrl-r, counts, `.` repeat (last change, not motion).
- V2 (text objects + search, ~3–4 days): iw/aw/iW/aW/is/as/ip/ap/ib/ab, `/` `?` n/N, * (word under cursor).
- V3 (registers/macros/marks, ~3 days): `"ayy`, `"ap`, `qaq@a`, `m{a-z}`, `'{a-z}`, jumps list.
- V4 (ex + composer bindings, ~2–3 days): `:w/:q/:wq/:e!/:s`, counts everywhere, status-bar mode
  indicator in composer (`-- NORMAL --` chip), `vim.enabled` setting + per-composer toggle.
- Total: ~12–16 days. Test strategy: `:domain` state-machine unit tests (transition tables —
  cheap, exhaustive), then on-device key-event tests.

## 4. Risks

- Soft-keyboard key events: Gboard sends `KEYCODE_UNKNOWN` for most letters (goes through IME
  commit path, not key events). Normal-mode letters (h/j/k/l) from soft keyboards may NOT arrive
  as key events → mitigation: custom input filter using `InputConnection` wrapper
  (`InputConnectionWrapper.commitText` interception) OR an on-screen vim key row. This is the
  highest-risk item — prototype V1 against Gboard on API 26 + current BEFORE committing to V2+.
- `onPreviewKeyEvent` + `TextFieldValue` cursor control is well-trodden (verified pattern).

## 5. Decision needed (user, before V1)

package dev.opencode.remote.chat

import android.content.Context
import android.graphics.BitmapFactory
import android.graphics.Bitmap
import android.net.Uri
import java.io.ByteArrayOutputStream

/** Staged attachment (H2): content resolved lazily at send time. */
data class StagedAttachment(
    val id: String,
    val uri: String,
    val filename: String,
    val mime: String,
    val sizeBytes: Long,
)

data class ResolvedAttachment(
    val filename: String,
    val mime: String,
    val dataUrl: String,
)

/**
 * Pure staging helpers (unit-tested). Compression policy (settings):
 * quality 0 = original bytes; 1 = JPEG q85 maxDim; 2 = JPEG q70 maxDim.
 */
object Attachments {

    fun isImage(mime: String): Boolean = mime.startsWith("image/")

    fun targetDim(maxDim: Int): Int = maxDim.coerceIn(320, 4096)

    fun jpegQuality(quality: Int): Int = when (quality) {
        1 -> 85
        2 -> 70
        else -> 70
    }

    fun buildDataUrl(mime: String, bytes: ByteArray): String =
        "data:$mime;base64," + java.util.Base64.getEncoder().encodeToString(bytes)

 package dev.opencode.remote.data.api
 
 import dev.opencode.remote.domain.AppSettings
 import dev.opencode.remote.domain.ServerProfile
 import kotlinx.coroutines.test.runTest

 import mockwebserver3.MockWebServer
 import org.junit.After
 import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
 import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
 import org.junit.Before
 import org.junit.Test
 
 /** Wire-contract tests: paths, Basic auth, bodies (mirror grapeot OpenCodeRepositoryTest). */
 class OpenCodeApiTest {
 
     private lateinit var server: MockWebServer
 
     @Before
     fun setUp() {
         server = MockWebServer()
         server.start()
     }
 
     @After
     fun tearDown() {
         server.close()
     }
 
     private fun api(user: String = "ucha", pass: String? = "secret") =
         ApiFactory.api(
             ServerProfile(id = "p1", name = "t", baseUrl = server.url("/").toString(), username = user),
             pass,
             AppSettings(),
         )
 
     @Test
     fun healthParses() = runTest {
         server.enqueue(MockResponse(body = """{"healthy":true,"version":"9.9.9"}"""))
         val h = api().health()
         assertTrue(h.healthy)
         assertEquals("9.9.9", h.version)
         val req = server.takeRequest()
         assertEquals("/global/health", req.target)
         assertEquals("Basic dWNoYTpzZWNyZXQ=", req.headers["Authorization"])
     }
 
     @Test
     fun promptAsyncPosts204WithAgentAndParts() = runTest {
         server.enqueue(MockResponse(code = 204))
         val res = api().promptAsync(
             "ses_1",
             PromptRequest(parts = listOf(PartInput(type = "text", text = "hi")), agent = "build"),
         )
         assertEquals(204, res.code())
         val req = server.takeRequest()
         assertEquals("/session/ses_1/prompt_async", req.target)
         val body = req.body?.utf8() ?: ""
         assertTrue(body.contains("\"agent\":\"build\""))
         assertTrue(body.contains("\"type\":\"text\""))
     }
 
     @Test
     fun permissionReplyUsesReplyField() = runTest {
         server.enqueue(MockResponse(body = "true"))
         api().replyPermission("prm_1", PermissionReply(reply = "once"))
         val req = server.takeRequest()
         assertEquals("/permission/prm_1/reply", req.target)
         assertTrue((req.body?.utf8() ?: "").contains("\"reply\":\"once\""))
     }
 
     @Test
     fun directoryInterceptorAppendsDirectory() = runTest {
         server.enqueue(MockResponse(body = """{"healthy":true,"version":"x"}"""))
         val profile = ServerProfile(
             id = "p1", name = "t", baseUrl = server.url("/").toString(),
             username = "u", defaultDirectory = "/home/u/proj",
         )
         ApiFactory.api(profile, null, AppSettings()).health()
         val req = server.takeRequest()
         assertTrue((req.target ?: "").contains("directory=%2Fhome%2Fu%2Fproj"))
     }
     @Test
     fun questionReplyPostsAnswers() = runTest {
         server.enqueue(MockResponse(body = "true"))
         api().replyQuestion("que_1", dev.opencode.remote.data.api.QuestionReply(listOf(listOf("A"))))
         val req = server.takeRequest()
         assertEquals("/question/que_1/reply", req.target)
         assertTrue((req.body?.utf8() ?: "").contains("\"answers\":[[\"A\"]]"))
     }
 
     @Test
     fun commandExecutes() = runTest {
         server.enqueue(MockResponse(body = """{"info":{},"parts":[]}"""))
         api().rawCommand("ses_1", dev.opencode.remote.data.api.CommandExecute(command = "init", arguments = "x"))
         val req = server.takeRequest()
         assertEquals("/session/ses_1/command", req.target)
         val body = req.body?.utf8() ?: ""
         assertTrue(body.contains("\"command\":\"init\""))
     }
 
     @Test
     fun catalogPaths() = runTest {
         server.enqueue(MockResponse(body = """{"all":[]}"""))
         api().rawProviders()
         assertEquals("/provider", server.takeRequest().target)
         server.enqueue(MockResponse(body = "[]"))
         api().rawAgents()
         assertEquals("/agent", server.takeRequest().target)
         server.enqueue(MockResponse(body = "[]"))
         api().rawCommands()
         assertEquals("/command", server.takeRequest().target)
     }
+    @Test
+    fun promptIncludesSystemModelVariantTools() = runTest {
+        server.enqueue(MockResponse(code = 204))
+        api().rawPromptAsync(
+            "ses_1",
+            dev.opencode.remote.data.api.PromptRequest(
+                parts = listOf(dev.opencode.remote.data.api.PartInput(type = "text", text = "hi")),
+                agent = "plan",
+                model = dev.opencode.remote.data.api.ModelInput("meta", "muse-spark-1.3"),
+                variant = "high",
+                tools = mapOf("webfetch" to false),
+                system = "Be brief.",
+            ),
+        )
+        val body = server.takeRequest().body?.utf8() ?: ""
+        assertTrue(body.contains("\"system\":\"Be brief.\""))
+        assertTrue(body.contains("\"variant\":\"high\""))
+        assertTrue(body.contains("\"webfetch\":false"))
+        assertTrue(body.contains("\"providerID\":\"meta\""))

 # opencode remote — GRAND PLAN (source of truth)
 
 > NEVER drift, regress, compact, or rewrite this file wholesale. Correct/add only, with user approval.
 > All phases, specs, and reviews argue from this file. Cross-check list: §11.
 > App name: "opencode remote"; launcher label: "opencode".
 
 ## 1. Vision & goals
 
 - G1: Match then beat Claude mobile app quality for remote opencode sessions (doc 01).
 - G2: Android-first, minSdk 26 support, easy + intuitive (docs 05, 08).
 - G3: Work from anywhere without PC — full PC-setup replacement: background tasks (P2),
   notifications (P1), extended widget (P3), background health (P4).
 - Quality over speed; no token/resource economy; research newest Android constraints always (Q1).
 - No Firebase/paid; on-prem only; blackwall + `uchabokeria.space`; no Tailscale (T4).
 
 ## 2. Locked decisions
 
 - D-Stack: 100% native Kotlin + Compose + M3 Expressive; minSdk 26; modules
   `:app/:feature/:domain/:data` (doc 06). Locked 2026-10-04.
 - D-Push: self-hosted ntfy + `serve→ntfy` bridge on blackwall + UnifiedPush in app + FGS fallback (doc 09).
 - D-Perms: fully aggressive first-run onboarding (direct battery-exemption request; Play risk accepted;
   sideload first). Decision D5 (docs 05, 13).
 - D-Temp (D2): temporary mode HIDES sessions locally (no server auto-delete) + purge action/setting.
 - D-Widget: extended — Claude 3 buttons + 3 recent shortcuts + status (locked round 3; no version cuts; phases = build order).
 - D-Vim: MAXIMAL emulation as own workstream (normal/insert/visual, motions+text objects, registers 0-9,
   macros, marks/jumps, :s, counts; library-first, expect custom InputConnection), non-blocking.
 - D-Push-T: per-device unguessable ntfy topics (locked round 3).
 - D1: Projects = client-side Room entity (memory/instructions per project) mapped to dirs,
   injected as system context. Server Project = directory only.
 - D3: websearch toggle = per-message tools gating; memory toggle = simple-memory injection on/off;
   permission default = PATCH /config rules; browser switch = /mcp + tools gating (verify live /doc).
 - D4: `/rc` + Tailscale flow keeps working until Tunnel cutover; then migrate.
 
 ## 3. Topology (no Tailscale)
 
 - `opencode.uchabokeria.space` → blackwall `serve :4096` via cloudflared Tunnel, per-server Basic auth.
 - `ntfy.uchabokeria.space` → self-hosted ntfy, native auth + unguessable topics, NO Cloudflare Access on machine endpoints.
 - `pc.uchabokeria.space` → reserved for PC tunnel later (post-v1 scope, design keeps the slot).
 - Secrets in EncryptedSharedPreferences + Keystore. `network_security_config.xml` dev allowlist only.
 
 ## 4. Research index (mobile/docs/)
 
 01-claude-app-ux · 02-ai-app-patterns · 03-third-party-clients (R11: alvarolorentedev UX + grapeot native;
 grinev bot for state machines; doza62 QR pairing) · 04-mobile-principles · 05-android-constraints
 · 06-stack-decision · 07-serve-api-contract · 08-ui-theming · 09-push-without-firebase
 · 10-browser-embed · 11-code-hygiene · 12-app-optimization · 13-settings-catalog (APPROVED round 3)
 · 14-r11-teardown (file-level, verified) · 15-permission-allowlist (DRAFT, needs approval).
 
 ## 5. Master feature list
 
 - S1 multi-server profiles + switching · S2 health/version pin · S3 retry/backoff/keepalive/resurrection + `?directory=` always
 - C1 list/search/open incl. PC-created · C2 new + temp mode (D2) + default-temp · C3 rename/fork/share/abort/revert/summarize/diff/todo/children
 - H1 Claude-like chat + streaming deltas · H2 attach files/images/camera (blocked: doc 07 gap #1 probe first)
   · H3 websearch default-on · H4 dictation + voice mode · H5 memory toggle · H6 connectors view
   · H7 permission cards Once/Always/Reject, unrestricted-default (allowlist doc 15 DRAFT) · H8 agent plan/ask/build
   · H9 model+effort server-driven picker · H10 stats tokens/$/context per-session + weekly
   · H11 projects (D1) · H12 slash commands native+custom · H13 vim full emulation (own workstream)
 - B1 browser per-chat enable · B2 playwright↔extension switch · B3 CDP screencast observe/control
   · B4 password handoff (Custom Tab + CredentialManager, FLAG_SECURE, revoke)
 - P1 ntfy push (reply-ready, approval stalls inline) · P2 FGS live sync · P3 extended widget
   · P4 background health screen
 - T1 theme engine day one · T2 dark/light/auto, default dark-cyberpunk neon (doc 08 tokens)
   · T3 user schemes import/export
 - X1 settings import/export · X2 biometric lock · X3 offline cache + resync · X4 QR pairing · X5 aggressive onboarding
 
 ## 6. Settings
 
 Catalog proposed in doc 13 — APPROVAL PENDING (consult round 3). DataStore-backed, JSON import/export.
 
 ## 7. Build order (phases, NOT version cuts — everything ships)
 
 - P0: scaffold (modules, DI, theme engine, settings infra, server profiles, health/version, S1–S3) + Tunnel plan
 - P1: sessions + chat + streaming (C1–C3, H1, S3 hardened) + upload probe (doc 07 gap #1)
 - P2: permissions/models/agents/commands/stats (H6–H10, H12) + connectors view
 - P3: attachments/voice/projects (H2–H5, H11) + H13 vim workstream (parallel, non-blocking)
 - P4: ntfy bridge + UnifiedPush + FGS + widget + health screen (P1–P4) + blackwall deploy
 - P5: browser/CDP/handoff (B1–B4)
 - P6: hardening — Doze/OEM matrix, API-26 + current lab, foldable, perf pass (doc 12), full regression
 - Each phase: implement → smoke-test on emulators (screenshots in-session) → cross-check vs this file
   → user review → real-device fix loop.
 
 ## 8. Hygiene & rules (docs 04, 11)
 
 MVVM+UDF, `:domain` pure, repos behind interfaces, Hilt, no GlobalScope, `prompt_async` sends,
 defensive parse, GET-then-merge config, tokens-only styling (lint), ktlint/detekt clean,
 tests (VM/repo unit + MockWebServer fake-serve + theme screenshots), no secrets in logs,
 FLAG_SECURE on sensitive surfaces. Never: perpetual bg SSE, polling loops, blind schema trust,
 plan rewrites.
 
 ## 9. Knowledge persistence
 
 `mobile/.remember/` handoff notes + memory entities (`opencode-remote-*`) + simple-memory.
 This repo's own `.remember` stays separate.
 
 ## 10. Open questions (spec phase, with user)
 
 ntfy topic/auth naming · default permission allowlist · browser-switch mechanism after /doc probe ·
 H2 upload path after probe · vim scope details · widget shortcut count · settings catalog approval (doc 13).
 
 ## 11. First-message cross-check (nothing dropped)

 · P1 flow→§7 · P2 root-clean (only .md/AGENTS.md at root) · P3 theme→T1–T3+doc08 · P4 name/perms→X5+D-Perms ✓
 · P5 persistence→§9 ✓. Root rule: project root holds only markdown/AGENTS/config; all code under feature modules.
